presentation.body: Spis shows every catalog in the installed corpus and the state it was measured at: record counts, the complete and partial split, image and structure counts, the provenance mix, and the files each catalog owns.
presentation.title: Read the reference corpus without opening a terminal

presentation.body: Browse reads the catalog index and runs the read-only checks — generate-example-catalogs --check, check-upstream-drift, verify-reference-evidence, capture-wisent-references --list. Docs searches the crawled pages. Crawlers and Manage change the corpus only by running its command line, so nothing in this window edits catalog files behind the corpus's back. Crawlers can also ask whether a host is ready for one product family before anything is claimed.
presentation.title: Browse and Docs report; Crawlers and Manage run the corpus's own commands

presentation.body: First use finishes only when a real catalog is on screen. Spis needs an installed corpus to read: with none found, this step states that instead of completing.
presentation.title: Open one catalog and read its measured state
